items.title: GitHub is proud to announce that you can now obtain your public repo on CD-ROM
items.author: throwaway2027
items.summary: GitHub now offers physical CD-ROMs of your public repositories, a nod to physical media trends. This service allows you to keep, share, or pass on your digital projects. Note that this is a unique initiative, not an official GitHub product.

items.title: Reality has a surprising amount of detail (2017)
items.author: vinhnx
items.summary: Reality has a surprising amount of detail, urging us to notice the unexpected nuances in everyday life, as highlighted by John Salvatier in 2017. This approach encourages deeper observation and understanding of the world around us.

items.title: Mystery identity of 'Green Boots' climber is finally solved after DNA test
items.author: FireBeyond
items.summary: The identity of the "Green Boots" climber on Mount Everest has been confirmed as Dorje Morup, an Indian climber, after 30 years of speculation. Previously, Tsewang Paljor was believed to be "Green Boots." The confirmation came through DNA testing.

items.title: FoundationDB's Flow – Bringing Actor-Based Concurrency to C++11
items.author: sourdecor
items.summary: FoundationDB's Flow is a C++11 extension that introduces actor-based concurrency. It uses new keywords and control-flow primitives to manage asynchronous functions. Flow compiles these functions into objects with sub-functions that use callbacks to avoid blocking.

items.title: Claude-real-video － any LLM can watch a video
items.author: cortexosmain
items.summary: Anthropic's Claude can analyze videos via a third-party skill called "Claude Video," which processes video frames and transcripts. This skill allows users to paste video URLs for analysis. It's not a native feature of the official Claude model.

items.title: The short leash AI coding method for beating Fable
items.author: Riseed
items.summary: The "short leash" AI coding method aims to leverage AI for high-quality software in security-critical systems with minimal human oversight. It emphasizes iterative reviews and human understanding of AI-generated code. This approach was developed by Greg Slepak.

items.title: A Special Wireless-Free Nikon Camera Is Publicly Available for the First Time
items.author: HardwareLust
items.summary: A special Nikon Z6 III camera without wireless connectivity is now available for the first time. It lacks Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, and is discounted by $700. This version is identical to the standard model but lacks wireless features.

items.title: Launch HN: Manufact (YC S25) – MCP Cloud
items.author: pzullo
items.text: Hi HN, we are Pietro and Luigi, cofounders of Manufact (https://manufact.com), a cloud for MCP apps and servers. We used to be called mcp-use, and still build open source SDKs for MCP under that name: https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use. We did a Show HN about that last year:
items.summary: Manufact is a cloud service for deploying and managing MCP applications, akin to Vercel for Next.js. It supports development, testing, and monitoring of MCPs. The platform aims to simplify interactions with AI products.

items.title: Show HN: ctx – Search the coding agent history already on your machine
items.author: luca-ctx
items.text:
Coding agents don't have long-term memory.

But you do have months of full-fidelity agent transcripts stored on your machine.

A simple solution that goes a long way: ingest those transcripts and logs into a structured SQLite database, then search them with ranked text match. Everything is fully local and doesn't require anything fancy like a graph database or hosted memory service.

This is the idea behind ctx, a Rust CLI that handles the ingestion and searching.

We give our agen
items.summary: ctx is a Rust-based CLI tool for quickly searching past coding agent sessions stored locally in SQLite. It indexes agent history for fast, scriptable searches without needing a background service.

items.title: Spain Orders Blacklist of Palantir from Public and Private Companies
items.author: mgh2
items.summary: Spain has banned Palantir from public and private companies due to national security concerns. The government aims to prevent misuse of classified information. Palantir still has contracts with the Spanish Ministry of Defense.

items.title: 24-bit/192kHz music downloads and why they make no sense (2012)
items.author: Kaapeine
items.summary: 24-bit/192kHz music downloads offer no benefits over standard formats and can have slightly worse fidelity. They consume significantly more storage without improving sound quality. This format is largely unnecessary for most listeners.

items.title: Android Developer Verification: Threat masquerading as protection
items.author: drewfax
items.summary: Android Developer Verification is criticized for being a threat instead of protection, with concerns about Google's control over app distribution. F-Droid argues it undermines open-source principles. This has sparked debate about app security and developer freedom.

items.title: AI can't be listed as inventor on patent applications, Japan's top court rules
items.author: mushstory
items.summary: Japan's Supreme Court ruled that AI cannot be listed as an inventor on patent applications, affirming that inventors must be natural persons. This decision upheld previous rulings by lower courts. The ruling applies to patents filed after the decision.

items.title: Client-side load balancing at a million requests per second
items.author: cjbooms
items.summary: Client-side load balancing at a million requests per second was achieved through an in-process load balancer, using consistent-hash routing and advanced techniques for cache warming and AZ-aware routing. This approach significantly improved latency and resilience.

items.title: Flexible metaprogramming with Rhombus
items.author: spdegabrielle
items.summary: Rhombus is a new programming language combining Racket's metaprogramming with simplicity. It offers advanced metaprogramming features for flexible code generation. The latest documentation provides a detailed reference for its metaprogramming capabilities.

items.title: Zuckerberg says AI agent development going slower than expected
items.author: cwwc
items.summary: Mark Zuckerberg stated that AI agent development is slower than expected. He also mentioned that recent company reorganizations have not been as effective as hoped. Meta plans to invest heavily in AI infrastructure.

items.title: NSA tries to weaken mlkem standardisation?
items.author: SuperSandro2000
items.summary: The NSA is not attempting to weaken ML-KEM standardization. DJB clarified that there are no known weaknesses in ML-KEM, and the IETF is working on a pure specification.

items.title: Is One Layer Enough? A Single Transformer Layer Matches Full-Parameter RL Train
items.author: tcp_handshaker
items.summary: Training a single transformer layer can achieve most of the gains from full-parameter reinforcement learning training, often surpassing it. This finding challenges traditional assumptions about the distribution of RL adaptation across transformer layers. The study shows that RL improvements are concentrated in a few layers, sometimes just one.

items.title: Show HN: CLI that helps AI agents avoid vulnerable dependencies
items.author: modelorona
items.text:
deptrust is a CLI that checks package versions for known vulnerabilities across npm, PyPI, crates.io, Go modules, RubyGems, NuGet, Maven, Packagist, pub.dev, CocoaPods, Hex.pm, Hackage, GitHub Actions, and more.

It runs locally as a CLI and as an MCP server. It calls public package registry and OSV APIs directly; there is no hosted deptrust service.

I built this because AI coding agents kept suggesting outdated or vulnerable package versions. I kept having to manually tell tools like Claude
items.summary: deptrust is a CLI tool that checks package versions for known vulnerabilities across various package managers. It helps AI agents avoid outdated or vulnerable dependencies. Install it via pnpx, brew, or go.
